text: This little brass robot has one job and that is to build a perfect copy of itself.
It reads the plans off a punched paper tape one row of holes at a time.
Each row tells it which part to grab and exactly where it goes.
The gears go in first and every single tooth has to mesh.
Its heart is a tiny balance wheel that ticks back and forth like a watch.
But a copy with no plans inside could never build anything.
So the very last thing it makes is a copy of its own tape.
A genius named John von Neumann worked out this trick in nineteen forty eight.
That was five years before anyone knew what DNA looked like.
And it is exactly what your cells do every time they split in two.
Now the new robot winds up and its tiny heart starts to tick.
Subscribe because that's how a machine could build itself.
